s1.syndrome_frame: progressive radicular pain and neuropathic symptoms in the lower extremity
salient_findings: radicular pain radiating from lower back down the left leg
mild hypesthesia in the left L5–S1 dermatome
cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone
key_facts: 8-month history of radicular pain
pain radiates from lower back down the left leg
occasional tingling
no weakness
no autonomic symptoms
no history of trauma or injury
mild hypesthesia in the left L5–S1 dermatome
normal muscle strength
normal abduction and adduction
negative Lasègue, Kernig, Bragard, and Sicard signs
electromyography shows neuropathic irritation of the left L4, L5, S1, and S2 roots
lumbosacral MRI shows a solitary, completely cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone
mass measures approximately 13.9 cm in length and 1.9 cm in maximal diameter
mass is hypointense on T1-weighted images and hyperintense on T2-weighted images
mass demonstrates peripheral rim enhancement

shortlist.label: Schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a solitary, completely cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone with peripheral rim enhancement, are consistent with a schwannoma, a type of nerve sheath tumor.

shortlist.label: Neurofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's presentation with progressive radicular pain and a cystic mass in the nerve root is also consistent with a neurofibroma, another type of nerve sheath tumor.

shortlist.label: Tarlov cyst
shortlist.why_kept: The cystic nature of the mass and its location in the nerve root are also suggestive of a Tarlov cyst, a type of cyst that can occur in the nerve roots.

shortlist.label: Ganglion cyst
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a cystic mass with peripheral rim enhancement, are also consistent with a ganglion cyst, a type of cyst that can occur in the nerve roots.

shortlist.label: Cystic schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a solitary, completely cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone with peripheral rim enhancement, are also consistent with a cystic schwannoma, a variant of schwannoma.

raw.rationale: The presence of a solitary, completely cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone that is hypointense on T1-weighted images and hyperintense on T2-weighted images, with peripheral rim enhancement, is most consistent with a Tarlov cyst. Additionally, the location and extension of the mass along the course of the sciatic nerve support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Schwannoma
rejected.why: Schwannomas are typically solid or mixed solid and cystic, not completely cystic

rejected.label: Neurofibroma
rejected.why: Neurofibromas are usually solid and may have a target sign on MRI, not a completely cystic mass

rejected.label: Ganglion cyst
rejected.why: Ganglion cysts are typically smaller and more superficial, not extending along a nerve root

rejected.label: Cystic schwannoma
rejected.why: While cystic schwannomas can occur, the completely cystic nature and specific imaging characteristics of the mass are more suggestive of a Tarlov cyst
